schemes.name: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)
schemes.eligibility: Landholding farmer families with cultivable land recorded in state land records, subject to the scheme's exclusion rules (higher-income categories are excluded). One registration per family.
schemes.benefits: Income support of Rs 6,000 per year in three equal instalments of Rs 2,000, paid directly into the bank account (DBT).
schemes.verified_note: Checked on 30 Oct 2026 against the PM-KISAN portal reference, a state government scheme page (wb.gov.in) and recent news reports. Instalment dates change; confirm on the portal.

schemes.name: PMFBY (Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana) - crop insurance
schemes.eligibility: Farmers growing notified crops in notified areas for the season, including sharecroppers and tenant farmers. Enrolment is voluntary. Notified crops, areas and last dates differ by state and season.
schemes.benefits: Insurance cover against crop loss from natural calamities, pests and diseases. Farmer pays up to 2% of the sum insured for Kharif food and oilseed crops, up to 1.5% for Rabi food and oilseed crops, and up to 5% for annual commercial and horticultural crops. The rest of the premium is subsidised by the Centre and the state.
documents: Land records or tenancy / sowing declaration
schemes.verified_note: Premium rates checked on 30 Oct 2026 across several sources. Enrolment last dates vary by state and season: check your state's notification.

schemes.name: Soil Health Card Scheme
schemes.eligibility: Farmers across India can have their soil tested through the scheme.
schemes.benefits: A soil health card with the nutrient status of your soil and fertilizer recommendations for your crops.
documents: Details of your land and crops (ask your local agriculture office)

schemes.name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
schemes.eligibility: Farmers who cultivate land, including tenant farmers and sharecroppers, as per the lending bank's rules.
schemes.benefits: Short-term credit for farming needs through your bank. Interest benefits may be available. Terms differ by bank.

schemes.name: e-NAM (National Agriculture Market)
schemes.eligibility: Farmers who sell produce through registered mandis connected to e-NAM.
schemes.benefits: An online trading platform that lets farmers see prices from connected mandis and sell to buyers across markets.
documents: Registration at your mandi or on the portal
